title: JSON output state, result publication, and extraction execution

scope.rationale: Post-retirement jsonStringGrow, jsonReturnString, and jsonReturnParse implementations plus JsonString error/reset, append, trim, termination, and separator routines form one dependency-closed output and result state machine. jsonAllAlphanum and the post-retirement jsonExtractFunc implementation consume it to execute ordinary and abbreviated paths, multi-path arrays, JSON/SQL result modes, JSONB output, result caching, and registered -> and ->> operators.
excluded_responsibilities: JsonString inline storage and reference-counted string allocation

dependencies.caller_closure: All fifteen assigned source bodies are complete. String growth owns sticky OOM/reset state; result publication selects text/JSONB, cache, subtype, and error branches; JSON text, aggregate, table-valued path, and extraction owners consume the state machine; registered json_extract, jsonb_extract, ->, and ->> execute the extraction dispatcher.

inputs: Borrowed bytes or one byte for append operations
Borrowed abbreviated extraction label for ASCII alphanumeric classification
outputs: Exact appended output, conditional comma, hidden zero terminator, or sticky output error
contracts.ownership: JsonString owns its dynamic buffer. Reset releases that allocation while preserving sticky error state; input slices remain borrowed.
contracts.state_and_results: OOM and too-deep publication clear output and remain sticky. Trim mutates only an error-free nonempty output. Termination appends a hidden zero then restores the logical length. Separator is a no-op for empty output or immediately after an opening container.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: No locks or I/O. SQL result callbacks remain in the calling JSON function owner.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Allocation failure records OOM and resets storage. Further growth fails while an error is sticky. Registered callers convert false/error state into SQLite result errors and remain safely destructible.

representation_differences: std.ArrayList replaces source inline zSpace plus reference-counted dynamic storage; reset releases the dynamic list and restores an empty list.
Three explicit booleans represent source eErr bits. Append functions return success booleans so typed callers publish SQLite errors without a context pointer in the core owner.
The hidden terminator occupies initialized capacity just beyond ArrayList.items after logical trim rather than being included in the slice length.
A bounded slice replaces source pointer-plus-length alphanumeric input.

The jsonExtractFunc declaration was rewritten after retirement of its no-credit path/name claim: its current declaration hash adds abbreviated integer/label/bracket paths, ->/->> mode dispatch, multi-path separation, and registered public operator execution and differs from the retired claimed hash.

The jsonStringGrow declaration was rewritten after retirement of its no-credit path/name claim: allocator failure now records sticky OOM, releases output storage, and prevents subsequent growth; its current declaration hash differs from the retired claimed hash.

The jsonReturnString and jsonReturnParse declarations were rewritten after retirement of their no-credit path/name claims: current code performs termination, sticky error ordering, cache insertion, reset, JSONB user-data dispatch, parse delta reset, and shared string publication and both declaration hashes differ from every retired claimed hash.

oracle.protocol: Construct output, exercise opening-container separator suppression, append two values with exactly one comma, terminate without changing logical bytes, reset and verify released storage, then publish too-deep and require sticky failure. Through prepared SQL, execute -> and ->> with alphanumeric labels and negative integer abbreviated paths.
internal_observations: operator result text and scalar quoting mode
oracle.normalization: Compare exact bytes, booleans, and prepared SQL result text.

assurance.oom: Allocator failure clears owned bytes, marks OOM, and is published by registered JSON callers.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: Connection-local output only; no I/O or shared state.
assurance.malformed_input: Raw append accepts arbitrary bytes. Abbreviated labels preserve source ASCII classifier and quoted fallback; malformed expanded paths remain lookup errors.
assurance.continuation: Error-free output remains appendable; sticky-error output rejects growth and remains safely reset/deinitialized.
assurance.performance: Capacity-aware raw and character paths preserve amortized linear construction and avoid per-byte allocation.

integration.production_owner: src/core/internal/json_core.zig output owner and src/core/internal/json_functions.zig registered SQL JSON owner
integration.native_call_path: JSON writers use shared append/growth; returnParse routes every JSON/JSONB edit result through user-data format selection and returnString cache/error/reset publication; registered extract functions execute ordinary and abbreviated path/result branches.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Private append-byte growth and duplicated comma conditions no longer bypass the source-shaped core owner.
